thought.text: Now let me apply a minimal fix to `init.sh` to make those two REVOKEs conditional on table existence:

reasoning_content: I need to modify these two REVOKE statements to use a DO block that checks if the table exists first before executing the revoke.

action.command:
cd /workspace && python3 - <<'PY'
import io
p='deployment/postgres/init.sh'
s=open(p).read()
old="""        -- Revoke access on model and route permissions
        REVOKE ALL ON model_permission FROM "$QGIS_DB_USER";
        REVOKE ALL ON route_permission FROM "$QGIS_DB_USER";
"""
new="""        -- Revoke access on model and route permissions (these tables are
        -- created by Django migrations and do not exist yet on a fresh
        -- install, so only revoke when they are present)
        DO \\\$\\$
        BEGIN
            IF EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM information_schema.tables WHERE table_schema='public' AND table_name='model_permission') THEN
                REVOKE ALL ON model_permission FROM "$QGIS_DB_USER";
            END IF;
            IF EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM information_schema.tables WHERE table_schema='public' AND table_name='route_permission') THEN
                REVOKE ALL ON route_permission FROM "$QGIS_DB_USER";
            END IF;
        END
        \\\$\\$;
"""
assert old in s, "old block not found"
s=s.replace(old,new,1)
open(p,'w').write(s)
print("patched")
PY
